paragraphs.text: 5.1 What We Are Testing and Our Main Goal

runs.text: 5.1 What We Are Testing and Our Main Goal

paragraphs.text: Imagine a student learning Python with an AI tutor. They only have a small amount of study time—a fixed study budget of B = 32.0 points (about four short lessons spaced days apart). Anyone can look smart right after reading an answer with hints. The real test of a good teacher is: when the student comes back weeks later with zero hints, do they still remember how to solve the problem?

runs.text: Imagine a student learning Python with an AI tutor. They only have a small amount of study time—a fixed study budget of B = 32.0 points (about four short lessons spaced days apart). Anyone can look smart right after reading an answer with hints. paragraphs.text: Main Outcome (Primary Metric): After studying ends, we give the simulated student fresh tests without any hints at 1 day, 7 days, and 30 days later (18 questions per day across 6 Python skills and 3 difficulty levels = 54 questions per student). Our main score is the mean delayed unaided pass rate (the average of Day 1, Day 7, and Day 30), and we highlight Day-30 retention separately because 30 days tests true lasting memory rather than short-term cramming. We compare our AI teacher against a standard rule-based teacher (Threshold Heuristic) using the exact same study budget and the exact same simulated students.

paragraphs.text: Monotonic GRU vs. Transformers & Time-Input GRU: In the earlier Retrospective (3-seed) run, monotonic_gru ranked #1 on validation selection (0.55175 vs. 0.55177 for time_input_gru).
